html:
SMTO-SKL-0079 — Microsoft 365 no longer accepts SMTO's sign-in

GUID: e0465988-7c4a-571d-89a6-439efb312f29
Slug: microsoft365-graph-unauthorized
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Microsoft rejected SMTO's sign-in for your account, even after SMTO renewed it. Your password may have changed or access was withdrawn. Microsoft refused this request, so it wasn't carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in a conversation to connect your Microsoft 365 account again, then open the sign-in link it shows. Signing in again gives SMTO fresh permission from Microsoft.
  2. On Microsoft's page, choose the same email address that was connected before and approve the request. SMTO only accepts the same account it had before, so your saved connection stays intact.
  3. If Microsoft says your account is blocked or needs a new password, sort that out with your IT team first. SMTO can't sign in while Microsoft is blocking the account.

What success looks like

  • SMTO says your Microsoft account is connected, and your request now completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to your Microsoft 365 administrator or the person who manages SMTO. Don't share your Microsoft password or sign-in codes in the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft Graph returned 401 Unauthorized again after SMTO's single token refresh, or a pre-authorized transfer URL (download redirect or upload session) returned 401.

What this means

  • Graph still rejects authorization after the supported refresh attempt, or returns an unauthorized response on a transfer path. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph still rejects authorization after the supported refresh attempt, or returns an unauthorized response on a transfer path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected account and recorded HTTP authorization response.

How to fix it

  • Run microsoft365.connection_status for the account_ref, then call microsoft365.connect with the same auth_app_ref and account_key so the same tenant and user re-consent; check in Microsoft Entra that the user and the app's consent are still enabled. A 401 on a transfer URL (download redirect or upload session) means that pre-authorized URL is no longer valid: start a new download, or inspect the destination before a new upload. Inspect any earlier unknown writes before repeating a mutation.
  • Inspect and restore authorization for the same account; reconcile earlier writes before repeating a mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account's supported authorization succeeds before more work.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
